title: Gold (GC) Analysis, Key-Zones, Setup for Mon (Nov 16)
description: Bias: The December gold contract settled at 3,886.3 on Friday, up 1.0 or 0.03 percent, after trading between 3,927.2 and 3,871.1, a 56.1 point range that sat inside Thursday's range. The flat settle ended a run of three consecutive lower settles and sits 1.0 above Thursday's 3,885.3, the lowest settle of the 260 sessions dated 11/03/25 through 11/13/26. Over five sessions the contract is down 188.6 points or 4.63 percent. The session high of 3,927.2 printed in the 10:30 PM ET bar on Thursday evening, the producer price index was released at 8:30 AM ET on Friday, November 13, 2026, per the verified forward calendar, with a monthly reading of 0.3 percent against a 0.4 percent forecast, and the session low of 3,871.1 printed in the 11:00 AM ET bar before the 1:30 PM ET settle. The dollar index rose 0.23 percent to 103.41 and the ten-year yield index closed at 5.15 after a 5.17 high, while the provider's market commentary attributed the dollar's strength to hawkish remarks from three regional Fed presidents, which is attributed commentary. Silver's December contract fell 1.89 percent and the gold to silver ratio rose to 79.12. On the gold tracking fund, the console places the largest gamma concentration and the primary put side support base together at 350, with the fund at 356, which this review treats qualitatively only. The composite multi-indicator read is "100% SELL" with strength "Strong" and direction "Strongest", unchanged from "100% SELL" a session earlier, against "32% SELL" a week ago. The settle sits beneath every settlement average from the 5-day to the 200-day, and the highs have fallen for four consecutive sessions. In this review's interpretation the bias is lower beneath Pivot R1 at 3,918.6, with a rebound toward Friday's 3,927.2 high the more likely first test and a retest of Thursday's 3,856.7 low the base case. Globex reopens at 6:00 PM ET on Sunday, so two days of headline exposure separate the settle from the next print, with Gulf headlines the main upside risk. Resistance: - 3,983.4 5-day settlement average - 3,974.7 Pivot R3 - 3,951.0 Pivot R2 - 3,940.4 9-day average stall level - 3,927.2 Friday's session high - 3,918.6 Pivot R1 - 3,895.0 9-18 day average crossing level - 3,894.9 Pivot Point Support: - 3,886.3 Friday's settle - 3,871.1 Friday's session low - 3,862.5 Pivot S1 - 3,856.7 Thursday's low, the 52-week low - 3,838.8 Pivot S2 - 3,828.2 published target price - 3,806.4 Pivot S3 - 3,787.9 one standard deviation support Primary Setup: SHORT the December contract from the 3,920 to 3,930 band, around Friday's 3,927.2 high and above Pivot R1 at 3,918.6. Stop 3,955, above Pivot R2 at 3,951.0 and the 3,940.4 stall of the 9-day average. Targets at 3,895 first, at the Pivot Point at 3,894.9, 3,865 second, above Pivot S1 at 3,862.5 and Thursday's 3,856.7 low, and 3,835 third, beneath Pivot S2 at 3,838.8. Risk to reward is roughly 1:1 to the first objective, 1:2 to the second and 1:3 to the third from the entry midpoint. The 14-day average true range is 91.7 points against a 30 point stop distance. A settle above Pivot R2 at 3,951.0 negates the thesis; two consecutive 30-minute closes above 3,930 remove the edge before the stop is reached. A weekend escalation in the Gulf or a reversal lower in the dollar can carry price through the stop in one move, which makes this an analyst judgment that rebounds toward Friday's high are sold. Friday's 3,886.3 settle held Thursday's level inside a narrow range near the 52-week low. In this review's interpretation Monday is a test of whether a rebound stalls beneath the 3,918.6 to 3,951.0 band, or whether a firmer dollar could carry the contract through Thursday's 3,856.7 low toward Pivot S2 at 3,838.8.

title: BTC Parked for the Weekend, Longs Haven’t Given Up
description: BTC Market Analysis | 2026.11.13 19:10 EST Market bias: Further downside is more likely, but price may range over the weekend before the next direction is set Key liquidation zones: Upside 69.1K / 71.4K / 74.0K / 75.2K; downside 67.6K / 65.0K Positioning: Stay on the sidelines. Watch OI and the long/short ratio over the weekend Expected path: Ranging around 67.6K–69.1K over the weekend while OI builds. Leaving room for a bounce depending on the long/short ratio Cumulative realized liquidations (11/13 06:35 – 19:10 EST, partial feeds from 4 exchanges): Longs $27.27M / Shorts $15.32M Liquidation map long/short ratio: 69.1% / 30.9% (All Leverage, full price range), down from 72.1% OI: Down from $7.01B to $6.71B on Kingfisher Funding rate: 0.0080%, rising again even as price fell CVD: Spot: Aggregate weakened sharply to −455M. Coinbase selling widened to −917M, and Binance also declined Futures: Aggregate −9.42B, a new low for the period Key indicators to watch: Changes in the long/short ratio, whether OI builds, funding rate, Coinbase spot CVD Reassessment trigger: A hold above 69.1K and spot turning to buying Review of the previous expected path Expected (11/13 06:35 EST): A bounce, then another leg down to retest the 68.2K and 67.5K areas. If PPI came in soft and spot buying picked up, short liquidations at 70.4K–72.3K could drive a bounce PPI note (11/13 08:45 EST): The PPI bounce seemed to hit the brakes; watch buying before deciding Actual: PPI headline came in below expectations, and price rose to 70.19K at 08:35 EST but never reached 70.4K. It then broke 68.2K at 10:35 EST, fell to 67.82K at 18:15 EST, and is now around 68.4K. Assessment: “A bounce, then another leg down to retest 68.2K” played out as written, and the call that the PPI bounce would be short-lived was right. Price did not reach 67.5K and stopped just above the 67.6K line. My take on the current situation Longs still don’t seem to have given up. Funding rose again even as price fell, and the long share on the liquidation map is still high in the 69% range. Longs keep coming in every time price drops. When longs truly give up, nobody wants to buy when it’s cheap, and people only line up when it’s expensive. Bottoms usually form when no one wants to buy, but right now there are still plenty of longs trying to buy the dip. That’s why I think further downside is more likely from here. For now, though, it feels like price has parked for the weekend. I’ll leave room for a bounce depending on how OI builds and how the long/short ratio shifts as price ranges through the weekend. Have a great weekend, and I’ll keep watching how things develop. For personal record and sharing only. This is not investment advice. Feedback and corrections are always welcome. Feel free to reach out! This is all fiction. Everything is a coincidence.

title: Avoiding Low Probability: Knowing When to Sit Out
description: Welcome to this educational breakdown focusing on a vital aspect of professional trading that many participants overlook : mastering the art of staying out of the market. Being profitable over the long term is not about taking trades every single hour; it is about protecting your capital and choosing only the highest probability setups. Even the best technical strategies will fail if applied during chaotic or low-probability market environments. Let us break down the exact logical scenarios when you should step aside and close your charts. Avoiding Choppy Consolidations and Ranging Markets Markets spend a large portion of their time in consolidation phases where price moves sideways without a clear institutional direction. During tight ranges or choppy price action, liquidity sweeps become unpredictable, and retail traders get trapped in false breakouts. If gold is grinding inside a messy range without clean structural displacement, it is always wiser to sit on your hands and wait for a decisive break of structure. Navigating High-Impact News Events Like FOMC Major macroeconomic catalysts, especially FOMC rate decisions, non-farm payrolls, or inflation data, bring extreme institutional volatility into the gold market. Smart money algorithms often use these high-impact news windows to sweep all resting liquidity on both sides before revealing the true direction. As a rule of thumb , it is best to avoid entering new positions right before a major news release or during the immediate liquidity spike. Give the market time to digest the news, print a clean structure, and show its hand. Monitoring SMT Divergence Between Correlated Assets When trading gold, comparing its behavior with related dollar assets or correlated indices can reveal hidden market truths. If you notice an SMT divergence—where correlated markets fail to confirm each other's highs or lows—it signals underlying weakness or institutional manipulation. Trading against a clear SMT failure drastically lowers your edge, and spotting this discrepancy is a strong technical cue to stay out. Waiting for High Probability ICT and SMC Confluence High-probability execution requires patience and alignment. Instead of chasing random moves, professional execution thrives when multiple ICT concepts align together. The best entries usually appear when a higher timeframe liquidity sweep is followed by a market structure shift, leaving behind a clean fair value gap (FVG). When price retraces respectfully into that aligned FVG with proper risk parameters, that is when the odds heavily favor the trader. Remember, preserving your emotional capital and account balance during bad market phases is just as important as capturing a winning trend. Trade smart, stay patient, and let the high-probability setups come to you. Disclaimer: This content is for educational purposes only and does not constitute financial advice.

title: Macro Bearish Divergence & "The Big Reset" Roadmap
description: After peaking near 7,820-7,850 in October, SPX (7,535) is testing the underside of its steep post-2023 ascending trend line on the monthly timeframe. While price carved out higher highs over the past two years, the underlying momentum histogram has printed a textbook macro bearish divergence, forming consistent lower highs since late 2024 and now rolling over right above the zero line. Macro Catalysts Supporting the Downside 1. Valuation & Rate Pressure (Supports Scenario 1) - Restrictive Yields: 10-year Treasury yields holding above 5.1% create severe multiple-compression pressure for equities at stretched valuations (Shiller CAPE near 40). - Hawkish Rate Expectations: Fed funds futures continue to price in sticky inflation and potential further tightening, removing the tailwind of rapid rate cuts. - Narrow Market Breadth: Rally concentration in mega-cap tech and semiconductors masks underlying weakness in the Equal-Weight S&P 500 and declining participation above the 200-day moving average. 2. Systemic & Liquidity Risks (Supports Scenario 2) - Energy & Inflation Shock: Sustained geopolitical disruptions keeping Brent crude above $100/bbl act as a direct tax on margins and consumer spending while keeping Core PCE elevated (~3.4%). - AI Capex Scrutiny: With hyperscalers committing $730B+ to AI infrastructure in 2026, any slowdown in ROI or order revisions poses a direct threat to index-level EPS growth. - Credit & Fiscal Friction: Renewed tariff headwinds and upcoming U.S. debt ceiling negotiations could tighten bond-market liquidity. (Key tell: watch High-Yield credit spreads and the 4.3% unemployment rate for signs of forced deleveraging). Two Downside Scenarios Scenario 1: Mean Reversion (5,700 - 6,000 | ~24-27% Correction) A rate-driven valuation reset pulls price down to test the rising blue moving average, clearing out excess leverage and resetting the monthly oscillator below zero without breaking the broader multi-year structure. Scenario 2: "The Big Reset" (4,612 - 4,850 | ~37-40% Drawdown) If energy inflation, an AI CAPEX slowdown, or widening credit spreads trigger an earnings contraction, price revisits the 2021-2022 cycle highs (~4,800), the major breakout shelf from early 2024, reinforced by the long-term green moving average.

description: Friday's regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) in NQ1! covered 703.75 points, about 131% of the 20-day average range of 537.25 and in the 85th percentile of recent sessions, per the RTH Range Gauge (free, open-source) on this 30-minute chart. Sellers pushed straight through the morning and the low printed in the 11:00 bar at 27,695.25, almost 700 points under the open. About 28,040: Friday's close, the middle of the afternoon recovery. 27,695: Friday's RTH low. 27,516: Tuesday's low and the low of the week. 28,697: Wednesday's high, the top of the week's range. If Monday's range passes about half of the 537-point average within the first hour, it would point to another wide day; a slow first hour under that pace would hint at a quieter, rotational session inside Friday's range. This is a market observation for education only, not a trade recommendation or financial advice.

title: Gold (XAUUSD): Bearish Break Below $3,860 Targets $3,590
description: Bias: Bearish Stance: I am looking to go SHORT on this setup, but only on confirmation. Trade Summary Direction: Short Entry Zone: Daily close (or 4H close with momentum) below $3,860 Stop Loss (Invalidation): $3,935 TP1: $3,770 (RR 1.2:1) TP2: $3,690 (RR 2.3:1) TP3: $3,590 (RR 3.6:1) Estimated Duration: 2–4 week swing trade All three targets pay more than the risk, so the trade passes the reward-over-risk filter. Market Structure & General Trend Gold’s daily structure is a textbook downtrend. The August 25 peak near $4,650 began a sequence of lower highs: roughly $4,490 in early September, $4,200 in October, and $4,150 in early November. Each rally has been weaker and has failed lower than the last. Lower lows confirm the sequence. Price is now trading in the $3,870–$3,890 area, the lowest of the period shown, and it has taken out the support that held through late October and early November. The Bollinger Bands (20, SMA, 2) confirm the trend. Price has spent most of the last two months below the $4,031 basis, and the basis itself has been sloping down since early September. In the first half of November, price was rejected at the basis and the upper half of the bands. Bulls could not even reclaim the mid-line. Technical Reasoning & Directional Call My call is a continuation lower once $3,860 gives way. The confluence behind it: Trend alignment: Lower highs, lower lows, and price below a falling 20-period basis. Trading with the dominant daily trend is the higher-probability side. Band walk: Today’s candle is pressing the lower Bollinger Band at $3,879. In a trending market, tags of the lower band tend to produce continuation. The band “walks” lower rather than marking a reversal. The earlier July range was different because the bands were tight and the market was basing. Here they are widening downward. Bearish momentum candle: Friday’s daily candle closed at $3,887, down about 1.07%, near its lows. It follows a large red candle on November 12 and an earlier strong rejection from $4,150. Sellers are showing conviction on the follow-through. Support cluster at $3,860–$3,890: Repeated tests weaken support. The more often a floor is touched, the fewer resting bids remain. A decisive close beneath it should trigger stops and open air below. RSI at 33: Momentum is weak but not yet oversold, so there is room for further downside before a classic exhaustion signal. RSI has made lower highs since September and failed to reclaim the 50 area on the November bounce. I see no bullish divergence. Price is making new lows alongside weak but confirming RSI. The key counterpoint is that price at the lower band with RSI in the low 30s can bounce. That is why I’m not shorting here. I want a close beneath support before committing. Approximate Price Path & Scenario Planning Primary scenario: Price consolidates or makes a minor bounce toward $3,920–$3,950, which is old support now acting as resistance. Sellers defend that zone, and price closes below $3,860, which triggers the entry. Price extends to TP1 at $3,770, where I’d expect a pause or small bounce. I’d take partial profit and move the stop to breakeven. Continuation toward TP2 at $3,690, with the lower band continuing to slope down. TP3 at $3,590 is a measured-move projection. The October–November range ran from about $4,150 to $3,880, roughly $270. Projecting that distance from the breakdown point gives about $3,590. There is no visible chart structure below current levels, so these targets rest on round numbers and measured-move logic rather than past reactions. Treat them as projections, not guarantees. Alternative scenario: If price bounces and consolidates above $3,860 without breaking, I stay flat. A bounce to the basis near $4,030 would be a better location to look for shorts. A reversal from there would offer a fresh setup with a clearer stop. Invalidation: A daily close above $3,935 negates the setup. It would mean the breakdown failed and that the Nov 12–13 selling was absorbed. A push back above the $4,031 basis would confirm bulls have regained control, and I would reassess my bearish bias entirely. Risk Management Risk is about $75 per ounce from entry to stop. I’d keep risk to 1% or less of account equity, sizing the position from the $3,860 entry and $3,935 stop. Scaling out at TP1 and TP2 and trailing the stop on the remainder would lock in gains while letting the trend work. Gold can gap on macro headlines, so avoid oversizing around scheduled economic releases. Disclaimer: This idea is for educational and informational purposes only and is not financial advice. Trading carries substantial risk of loss. Always do your own research and manage risk according to your own circumstances. If you found this useful, a like and a follow are appreciated, and I’d be glad to hear your own levels in the comments.
